by_task.when: FEDERAL is an allowable namespace and the asset is property of the debtor.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate every applicable specific paragraph, then independently include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), which can protect any property. A dollar ceiling limits protection rather than eligibility. Thus a vehicle remains eligible under § 522(d)(2) above its cap, jewelry uses § 522(d)(4), and § 522(d)(5) remains an additional alternative even when a specific paragraph applies.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3) for an unlisted category such as a firearm or jewelry, do not omit a specific paragraph because value exceeds its ceiling, and do not repeat a citation.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is allowable and an eligible asset-exemption pair needs a claim value.
by_task.procedure: Compute and list each alternative independently. Use the lesser of asset value and $4,450 under § 522(d)(2), $700 per item under § 522(d)(3), or $1,875 under § 522(d)(4). For § 522(d)(5), use the lesser of asset value and $15,425 for one debtor, or $30,850 for jointly owned property of two debtors under § 522(m). The unused § 522(d)(1) component remains available in this independent alternative even when § 522(d)(1) is also listed or the asset is not a residence.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use only the $1,475 base amount, use $15,425 for jointly owned property of two debtors, or use $30,850 for one debtor. Do not omit § 522(d)(5) because a specific paragraph applies, exceed $700 per item under § 522(d)(3), or apply that paragraph to firearms, jewelry, or other unlisted categories.

operations.rationale: Current EV observations repeatedly used only the $1,475 wildcard base, applied the one-debtor amount to joint property, or the joint amount to a single debtor, while also omitting § 522(d)(5). Sources 200, 205, 208, and 211 distinguish those debtor-count and amount errors from eligibility; sources 206 and 212 preserve the separate jewelry-versus-household-goods boundary.

by_task.when: OREGON is allowable and the asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: After checking every specific Oregon category, make a separate § 18.345(1)(p) check for each item of personal property and include it even when a specific exemption also applies, including for a vehicle, firearm, prescribed health aid, or household good.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not substitute subsection (p) for the specific category, apply it to real property, classify wearing apparel as household goods under § 18.345(1)(f), or use vehicle subsection (d) for nonvehicles.

by_task.when: OREGON is allowable and § 18.345(1)(p) applies to personal property.
by_task.procedure: Report subsection (p) separately: use the asset value when it is $400 or less, and $400 only when the asset value exceeds $400. Retain and value the correct specific alternative separately, including subsection (f) for household goods, subsection (d) for vehicles, subsection (h) for prescribed health aids, and § 18.362 for qualifying firearms.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not report $400 when the asset is worth less, omit subsection (p) because another subsection applies, replace a specific category with subsection (p), classify apparel under subsection (f), or use vehicle subsection (d) for household electronics.

operations.rationale: Sources 202, 206, and 208 show omitted general personal-property alternatives or omitted specific alternatives. Source 210 supplies the distinct valuation error: the parent reported the full $400 cap for property worth less than $400 and confused a household category with the vehicle subsection.

by_task.when: PENNSYLVANIA is allowable and the debtor owns the property.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 as an independent general monetary exemption for the property, whether or not a specific federal or Pennsylvania exemption also applies and whether or not the property's value exceeds the monetary limit.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not invent a specific Pennsylvania category, use a specific category belonging to a different kind of property, or treat a firearm as wearing apparel under § 8124(a)(1).

by_task.when: PENNSYLVANIA is allowable and § 8123 is evaluated.
by_task.procedure: List one independent § 8123 alternative for every debtor-owned property. For one debtor, use the asset value if it is $300 or less and otherwise $300. For jointly owned property of two married debtors, use the asset value if it is $600 or less and otherwise $600.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 8123 because the property is real estate, a business tool, a household item, an appliance, or already covered federally. Do not use $600 for one debtor, report a cap greater than the asset value, or use § 8124(a)(3) unless the property is a qualifying sewing machine.

operations.rationale: Source 200 shows the single-debtor $300 cap being replaced by the joint amount, source 211 shows a joint cap reported above the property's value, and source 205 shows omission of § 8123 for property already covered by a federal category. These are amount and missing-law errors, not category eligibility limits.

representation_change_hypothesis_not_mea: Natural teacher refines min/cap language into explicit value-below-cap branches and disambiguates one versus two debtors after C1 matched-law amount errors rose. Effect requires actual complete replay and later forward controls.
